job.theme: the life of a famous Indian scientist
job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: October 12, 2023. Today, our science teacher, Mr. Sharma, told us about the brilliant Sir C.V. Raman. I was amazed to learn that he was born in Tiruchirappalli on November 7, 1888. Raman was fascinated by the deep blue color of the Mediterranean Sea while traveling on a ship in 1921. He wondered why the water appeared so blue, which led him to study how light scatters when it hits molecules. Because he observed this light scattering effect, he eventually discovered the 'Raman Effect' in 1928. This discovery proved that light changes its wavelength when passing through a transparent medium. I read that he won the Nobel Prize in 1930 for this work. My friend Anjali thinks he discovered the effect because he was on a boat, but Mr. Sharma explained that the discovery happened because of his rigorous experiments in his laboratory in Kolkata. It is inspiring to think how a simple observation during a sea voyage changed the history of physics forever. I hope to visit his lab in Kolkata someday to see where he worked. Even though he was a busy scientist, he always found time to encourage young students like us to observe nature closely.
response.summary: This diary entry reflects on the life and scientific achievements of Sir C.V. Raman. It highlights how his curiosity about the sea led to the discovery of the Raman Effect.
